display.title: Eliyahu HaNavi's Surprise Visit
display.summary_short: A poor family refuses to sell their heirloom cup of Eliyahu HaNavi, and a beggar's silver coin that keeps coming back fills their home for Pesach.
display.summary_long: After the song 'I Believe in Hashem', the storyteller tells of Naftali and Esther, a poor couple who never lose their bitachon. Year after year they sell whatever they own to pay for each Yom Tov, until two weeks before Pesach nothing is left but a golden, jeweled cup inscribed 'Eliyahu HaNavi', handed down for generations. Esther and the children will not let Naftali sell it. While he says Tehillim in shul, a starving old beggar knocks; Esther gives him her last dry slice of bread, and as he leaves he gives her a silver coin. Every time she buys something for Pesach, the coin is back in her apron pocket, and soon the house is stocked, the children are dressed in new clothes, and the house is painted and decorated. Naftali comes home and thinks he has the wrong house. At the Seder, when they open the door, the beggar appears in splendor as Eliyahu HaNavi and blesses them, but Naftali has dozed off. On the second night he dozes off again, and Eliyahu explains that he showed himself to the family because they honored his cup, promising that everyone will see him soon with Moshiach.
display.lesson: Trust in Hashem even when things look hopeless, share what little you have, and honor what is holy.

advisories.note: A poor family must sell their belongings to pay for Yom Tov.
